# Welcome {.unnumbered}

Welcome to the **Hawaiʻi CKMR Workshop 2026**, taught by Mark Bravington and Eric Anderson.

This is our course web page: a clearinghouse for links to the slides, exercises, code, data, and other materials you will need. We will update it as the workshop goes along. Many of the materials will be hosted on the instructors' GitHub pages or in their GitHub repositories; we will introduce them and add links here as we use them.

## Prepare your laptop

Please prepare R and the packages for both instructors' hands-on exercises before the workshop. **R 4.6.x is the recommended starting point**, with pre-built packages for a broad range of supported Mac and Windows systems. Mark's packages also have builds for other R versions, including **R 4.5.x on Mac and Windows**; see his setup page for the platform/version options.

Installation commands for required packages can be run in the **R console**.  See
the following links for explicit commands.

- [Install packages for Mark's hands-on exercises](mark-setup.qmd)
- [Install packages and prepare for Eric's hands-on exercises](eric-setup.qmd)

## Do some pre-workshop reading

This course is intended to provide a "cold start," meaning we build up CKMR
concepts from their foundations without requiring prior knowledge. Nonetheless,
if you wish to read up on CKMR before the workshop, or during your flight to
Hawaiʻi, we recommend two readings, each with a different flavor.

* If you enjoy mathematical statistics and notation, the fundamentals of CKMR are
  laid out in those terms in [Bravington, Skaug, and Anderson (2016). Close-kin mark-recapture. _Statistical Science_ 31:259-274](https://projecteuclid.org/journalArticle/Download?urlId=10.1214%2F16-STS552). 
* For a more accessible introduction to CKMR, we recommend [Bravington and Carroll (2023). The practical magic of close-kin mark-recapture. CSIRO Publishing (download PDF)]({{< var mark-repo-url >}}/raw/refs/heads/master/brav-2025-carroll-chapter-11-CKMR.pdf). To download it, accept Mark's emailed invitation to his private GitHub repository and sign in with the GitHub account associated with that invitation.

**Essential reading:** Please read [Mark's 2026 R cribsheet (PDF)](background/rcrib26.pdf).
Reading this ahead of time can help immensely.  Mark has developed an R ecosystem
of packages and functions, and he relies on R environments for computational efficiency
and syntactic brevity.  This may be unfamiliar to some R users.  His cribsheet
provides an essential introduction.  

## BYOS — Bring your own species

The workshop agenda includes worked examples for a series of different species that
illustrate real-life scenarios.  In addition, the extended nature of the course is intended
to provide participants with a chance to apply principles of CKMR design to their
own species of interest.  For such design, it is not necessary to know everything,
but we provide brief [BYOS guidelines](byos-guidelines.qmd) for key pieces of
information you'll want to be armed with.  

## Workshop agenda

The current agenda is below. Exactly what happens when is flexible: we will adjust to the pace of the workshop. The three additional workshop days after the formal course offer a chance to explore topics more deeply and to work on specific fisheries/species of interest.

[Download the original agenda (PDF)](background/agenda-v1.pdf)

### Monday, November 9

- **Introduction:** principles, scope, and workshop overview
    + [Mark's intro slides (must be member of repo)](https://github.com/markbravington/hawaii-ckmr-26/blob/master/slides-etc/intro26b.pdf)
    + [Space-toast slides](background/space-toast.pdf)
- **Parent-offspring pairs (POPs):** simple marine mammal example and model
    + [Mark's _Delfinus mendax_ slides (must be member of repo)](https://github.com/markbravington/hawaii-ckmr-26/blob/master/slides-etc/delfi26.pdf)
    + Delfi_A: ideal data scenario (in `hawaii-ckmr-26` at `./r-scripts/fit_delfi_A.r` )
    + Tidyverse version of delfi_A in CKMRshiny [(here)](https://github.com/eriqande/CKMRshiny/blob/main/tidy_rmd_examples/fit_delfi_A.Rmd)
- **Gotchas #1:** because nothing is ever that simple…
    + Heritable covariate that affects sampling: `fit_delfi_B.r`
    + POPs, unequal reproduction, size selectivity, etc.  [Eric's CKMRshiny app with POPs](https://github.com/eriqande/CKMRshiny)

### Tuesday, November 10

- **Half-sibling pairs (HSPs):** shark example
- **Gotchas #2:** HSPs are a rich source of gotchas
- **And so to fish:** basic CKMR-driven fish model
- **Genetics and kin-finding #1:** principles

### Wednesday, November 11

- **Finishing up genetics** (8:30-11:00)
    + Maternal DNA
    + Epigenetic aging
    + Genetic sex identification
        - For genetically determined sex
        - Even for environmentally determined sex (using epigenetics)

- **Kinference** (11:00-12:00)
    + [Mark's kinference slides (must be member of repo)](https://github.com/markbravington/hawaii-ckmr-26/blob/master/slides-etc/Kinference26.pdf)
    + Shane Baylis's School Shark demo of Kinference (link not yet available)
- Fish:
    + [Mark's _Notogorgius_ slides (must be member of repo)](https://github.com/markbravington/hawaii-ckmr-26/blob/master/slides-etc/Notog-1-26.pdf)
- **Missing/uncertain data:** usually this means age
- **Fish:** a semi-realistic model. The 3rd loop?
- **Case study #1:** school sharks
- **Kin-finding and genetics #2:** worked examples

### Thursday, November 12

    + Sidebar:  Mark B:  a few more fish CKMR things.
